{
  "title": "The Keeper's Lantern",
  "world": "Cinematic Storybook Realism",
  "cold_open": "The salt air tastes of iron and ancient brine. Tonight, the gale screams against the jagged teeth of the coast.",
  "question": "Why does the lighthouse beam cut through the fog, when the oil has been dry for thirty years?",
  "journey": "Elias climbed the spiral stairs, his boots clicking against stone worn smooth by a century of toil. He carried a heavy lantern of his own, but its flame flickered weakly against the draft. Above, the great glass housing groaned. The gears—rusted, seized, and choked with dust—began to turn with a low, rhythmic hum that vibrated in his chest. It wasn't the mechanical grind of metal, but a steady, intentional rotation, slicing the darkness into ribbons of gold and shadow.",
  "discovery": "He reached the gallery and stopped. There, in the center of the great lens, burned a flame of impossible clarity. It didn't hiss; it breathed. It cast a warmth that didn't just illuminate the room, but softened the edges of the peeling paint and the lonely shadows of the rafters.",
  "emotional_turn": "Elias reached out, his trembling fingers hovering near the heat. He saw a faint silhouette in the reflection of the glass—not a ghost, but a memory of a man whose hands were still calloused by the sea. A steady, loving gaze.",
  "payoff": "The light wasn't a haunting; it was a promise kept. As long as the storm raged, the old keeper’s duty remained. The lamp stayed lit to guide the lost home, a silent vigil held by a spirit who refused to let the coast go dark.",
  "after_image": "A single, steady beam of gold finds its way across the white foam of the waves.",
  "hero_shot": "A weathered hand resting on a railing, bathed in a golden glow that feels like a warm embrace."
}
